profiles.name: Dorothy Kirsten
profiles.excerpt: Dorothy Kirsten was one of the Metropolitan Opera's leading American sopranos, bringing operatic technique and star presence to radio concerts and musical drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Dorothy Kirsten was born in Montclair, New Jersey in 1910 and developed into one of the leading American operatic sopranos of her generation. After early study in the United States, she continued her training in Europe and built a career that eventually made the Metropolitan Opera her principal stage home for three decades.

Kirsten's radio appearances were extensions of that musical career rather than character acting assignments. On programs such as The Railroad Hour, she performed operetta and musical-theatre material for a national audience, translating the projection and phrasing of the opera house to the intimacy of the microphone.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 26 The Railroad Hour broadcasts featuring Kirsten. Her public profile is therefore classified with singers and vocalists, where those performances accurately reflect the profession for which she was known.
